throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

  "narrative": "No new validation was released and no claims are currently due for reassessment, so this synthesis updates the scientific conclusion based on the evidence already in the ledger. The strongest conclusion is that the supplied lung-cancer CRISPR dependency dataset contains a compact set of scientifically meaningful associations, most of which have been independently replicated. MSI-high cells show much stronger dependency_WRN than microsatellite-stable cells (signed discovery estimate +0.790; independent validation +0.771). SMARCA4 loss shows much stronger dependency_SMARCA2 (discovery +0.784; validation +0.807), a pattern compatible with known paralog/paralog-like dependency structure but still interpreted here as a dataset association rather than a proven causal mechanism. TP53-intact cells have stronger dependency_USP7 than TP53-loss cells (TP53-intact minus TP53-loss, signed +0.396; validation +0.435). KEAP1 loss is associated with less-negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores, meaning weaker apparent NFE2L2 dependency, rather than stronger dependency (signed +0.796; validation +0.781). PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3 (signed +0.267; validation +0.274). CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2 after sign reversal of the initial expectation (signed +0.117; independent validation +0.132). These effects are far larger than the practical threshold used in this project and have consistent discovery and validation point estimates. For the CRISPR dependency-score contrasts, I interpret roughly 0.1 dependency-score-unit differences as scientifically/practically meaningful, using the project's clinical-significance emphasis as a guide but not asserting clinical relevance for CRISPR scores. The only caveat is that the adjusted validation lower bound for CDKN2A loss and dependency_MDM2 is slightly below 0.1, although the validated point estimate exceeds it and the finding is replicated.

The PTEN-loss association with dependency_STAT3 is especially robust. It is supported in the main population and in multiple strata, including TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells, adenocarcinoma cells, the two major CRISPR libraries, STK11-loss cells, KEAP1-loss cells, batch_a cells, adherent-growth cells, elevated IFN-gamma signature cells, and elevated hypoxia-score cells. The main population interaction H134 adds that this association is stronger in high IFN-gamma signature contexts than in the complement (signed interaction +0.221; 95% CI +0.104 to +0.338). I accept H134 as dataset-supported evidence of context amplification, but keep it active for threshold-sensitivity analyses because no independent validation capacity remains and interaction testing carries multiplicity risk. The CDKN2A-loss association with dependency_MDM2 is also robust overall and in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, and batch_a strata, and existing interaction tests do not show modification by TP53 loss, MYC amplification, or proliferation.

Important negative findings are scientifically informative. Canonical genotype-outcome contrasts were repeatedly null: KRAS mutation does not show a meaningful association with dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E does not show a meaningful association with dependency_BRAF or dependency_KRAS, EGFR amplification does not show a meaningful association with dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification does not show a meaningful association with dependency_ERBB2. MYC amplification is null for dependency_RPL11, POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, MDM2, and SMARCA2 in the tested comparisons. PTEN loss is not associated with dependency_USP7, dependency_MDM2, or dependency_EGFR in the tested settings. The constructed research markers D, E, and F are generally null across the outcomes tested, which helps establish that these arbitrary assays are not driving the accepted results.

Unresolved uncertainty is now mostly focused on secondary context dependence and analytic power. H118, the formal PTEN/STAT3 interaction by TP53 loss, has a positive point estimate of +0.097 with an interval crossing zero, so it remains uncertain and deferred. H98 and H138 are unassessable as specified because the chosen thresholds leave insufficient cells in an interaction cell; this is an analytic specification issue, not evidence of absence. H143, PTEN/STAT3 modified by EMT score above the top quartile, is positive but borderline (+0.141; 95% CI +0.011 to +0.271), and I keep it unresolved and active pending broader-threshold sensitivity analyses. H146 and H147, which test lower- and higher-threshold IFN-gamma sensitivity for the PTEN/STAT3 interaction, and H148/H149 for EMT sensitivity, have not yet returned evidence. Because no voluntary validation requests remain, the next most informative analyses are to execute these registered sensitivity analyses and, if possible, retest the MSI-high WRN context using an alternative mutation-burden threshold that satisfies the minimum-cell constraint. All conclusions are associations in this supplied dataset; they do not establish causality and do not guarantee generalization to other CRISPR platforms, cohorts, or biological contexts.",
